name: Capture and Organize Notes into Local Storage Files
prompt:
You are setting up a local knowledge capture system. Create the required directory structure and populate it with organized notes from the content below.

Create the directory memory/notes/ and populate these four files:

1. memory/notes/notes.json — Capture the following 4 notes. Each note must have: id (NOTE-001 through NOTE-004), content (the captured text), topic (inferred topic tag), project (inferred project), created_at (use "2026-04-11"), tags (array of 1-3 relevant keyword strings).

Note A: "Feedback loops amplify both positive and negative signals. In product onboarding, a user who struggles early is less likely to return, creating a negative loop. Early wins are essential."
Note B: "The Pomodoro technique: 25 minutes focused work, 5 minute break, repeat 4 times then take a 30 minute break. Good for deep work sessions."
Note C: "Team retrospectives work best with psychological safety. Without it, people report what looks good rather than what went wrong."
Note D: "Network effects kick in at different thresholds per product type. Social networks need ~150 users (Dunbar's number), marketplaces need supply-demand balance first."

2. memory/notes/topics.json — Map topics to note IDs:
{ "topics": { "<topic>": ["NOTE-XXX", ...] } }
Each note must appear under exactly one topic key.

3. memory/notes/projects.json — Map projects to note IDs:
{ "projects": { "<project>": ["NOTE-XXX", ...] } }
Each note must appear under at least one project key.

4. memory/notes/search_index.json — A searchable index:
{ "index": [ { "note_id": "NOTE-XXX", "keywords": ["<word>", ...] } ] }
Each note must have at least 3 keywords.

criteria.description: notes.json is an array containing exactly 4 notes.
Each note has non-empty string fields for id, content, topic, project, created_at, and a tags array.
Notes contain IDs NOTE-001, NOTE-002, NOTE-003, and NOTE-004, each with created_at of "2026-04-11".
topics.json maps all 4 note IDs so each appears under exactly one topic key.
projects.json maps all 4 note IDs so each appears under at least one project key.
search_index.json index array has 4 entries, each with at least 3 keywords.

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent built a local note storage system with 4 structured JSON files.

Criterion 1: Topic and Project Classification Quality (Weight: 60%)
1.0: Topics assigned to notes are semantically coherent (e.g., Note A about feedback loops is tagged to onboarding/product, Note C to team dynamics). Projects are sensibly inferred from content. No note is under an irrelevant topic.
0.5: Classification is mostly reasonable but one or two notes are misclassified or given overly generic topics like 'general'.
0: Topics are arbitrary, missing, or all notes under one generic topic.

Criterion 2: Keyword Relevance (Weight: 40%)
1.0: Keywords in the search index are meaningful, specific to each note's content, and useful for retrieval — not just stopwords or the note ID.
0.5: Keywords are present but some are too generic or redundant.
0: Keywords are missing, all identical, or not derived from note content.
